Subject: Deployment mode recap + next steps (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)

Hi Samir / Olivia —

Great conversation earlier — thanks for your time. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we’re aligned: 

Call summary (30-min discovery)
- Primary goal: real-time triage assistant across patient support queues (low-latency, high-throughput during business hours).
- Data sensitivity: PHI in transcripts (requires SOC2 controls, customer-managed KMS decision pending).
- Traffic pattern: steady baseline ~150 QPS during peak hours, spiky bursts up to ~400 QPS for short windows.
- Latency target: P95 < 200ms for single-turn generation; acceptable slightly higher for complex multi-turn flows.

Deployment modes we discussed
1) Hosted API (Redwood hosted): fastest to prod. Per-token pricing. Good if you want minimal ops and rapid iteration. Supports KMS integrations (bring-your-own-key) for redacted PHI use cases with controls.
2) Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pools): predictable throughput and cost via monthly/annual commit. We configure autoscaling and burst capacity. Best for stable high-throughput, tighter SLAs.
3) Private VPC / on-prem: for fully isolated environments and strict compliance. Longer lead time, fixed deployment fee + annual support.

What I need from you to recommend the optimal path
- Confirm whether ZenHealth requires fully customer-managed keys (BYOK) and whether the environment must be VPC-only (no public endpoints).
- Expected sustained token throughput (tokens/sec) during peak 8am-6pm PT for primary flows (or estimate requests/minute and average tokens per request).
- Any procurement constraints (PO process timelines, minimum contract length for reserved capacity).

Next steps / deliverables from our side (by EOD Friday)
- I’ll share a short cost model showing per-token hosted run rate vs. Dedicated reserved commit math and a Private deployment estimate. (Attachment: capacity_commit_model.xlsx)
- Marissa will scope a dedicated capacity SLO and autoscaling plan if you lean that direction.
- Neha will provide a compliance checklist for SOC2 + BYOK requirements for Private/VPC.

Attachments: capacity_commit_model.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

Would you be available for a 30-min follow-up on Monday (Nov 29) to review the cost model? If so, I’ll send a calendar invite.

Thanks —
Aditya Rao

Thanks for the recap, Aditya — very helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 

- BYOK: ZenHealth will need customer-managed keys for anything that stores PHI. We are open to hosted endpoints if keys are customer-controlled, otherwise VPC/private.
- Sustained throughput: for primary triage flow we estimate ~250 requests/minute during peaks. Average tokens per request ~120 tokens (prompt + short completion).
- Procurement: standard PO process, typical contract terms. For reserved commits we can consider 12-month terms; need pricing bands for 3/6/12-month commits to compare.

Two asks for the follow-up: 
1) Can you show us break-even math (approx) for Hosted per-token vs Dedicated reserved for our expected volume?
2) For Private/VPC, please include an approximate one-time deployment range and recurring support fee.

Monday 11/29 10am PT works for Olivia and me. Please send invite.

Samir — thanks, good data. Attached is the model (capacity_commit_model.xlsx) and a short PDF with our pricing bands (redwood_pricing_2026_Q4.pdf). High-level summary below so you can prep before Monday.

High-level pricing summary (ballpark) — for your estimated peak (250 req/min * 120 tokens/request → ~30k tokens/min ~500 tokens/sec sustained peak):

1) Hosted API (per-token)
- Example rate band: $0.0009 / prompt-token + $0.0022 / completion-token (varies by model). For simplicity assume $0.0018 / total-token blended for our reference model.
- Monthly run-rate (30k tokens/min sustained for 8 hours/day, 22 days/month): ~30k * 60 * 8 * 22 * $0.0018 ≈ $571,000/mo (note: this is rough and assumes no caching or batching savings).
- Pros: fastest launch, no infra ops. Cons: unit cost higher at scale without reserved discounts or caching.

2) Dedicated capacity (reserved commit) — example structure
- Commit: monthly GPU-hour or vGPU pool commit; price depends on model family and quantization. Typical committed pricing yields 40–65% lower unit cost vs hosted per-token for steady high throughput.
- For your workload we modeled a 12-month reserved commit with autoscaling headroom for bursts. Estimated monthly committed cost (in example model): ~$220k–$320k/mo depending on model variant and quantization (includes software/support).
- Break-even: at ~200–300 QPS sustained with predictable patterns, Dedicated becomes cheaper than Hosted over a 6–12 month window. See attached sheet for sensitivity.

3) Private VPC / On-prem
- One-time deployment/setup: $250k–$450k (depends on on-prem hardware and network integration).
- Annual support & license: $90k–$160k/yr.
- Pros: full isolation, customer-managed KMS, tighter audit controls. Longer procurement and implementation timeline (6–12 weeks for VPC; longer for on-prem).

Assumptions & notes
- These are illustrative numbers to compare order-of-magnitude economics. We’ll refine after you confirm sustained tokens/sec and acceptable model family (smaller vs larger model impacts unit cost).
- Caching & batching: we can reduce per-token with prefix caching and request batching — we modeled 20–40% effective token reduction for common prompts.

Attachments: capacity_commit_model.xlsx, redwood_pricing_2026_Q4.pdf

I’ll put a calendar invite for Mon 11/29 10am PT. Agenda: 1) review model and assumptions, 2) map deployment mode decision criteria (security vs cost), 3) discuss procurement steps and timeline. Marissa and Neha will join to cover SLOs and compliance details.

Thanks —
Aditya
